main_body: Seamless dark grey-brown cobble/plate ground texture, a flat terrain patch with a repeating pattern and no standing volume
top_band: none; the column scan shows a repeating texture pattern, not a top band over a front face
evidence: The kind is terrain: a flat ground tile pattern, not a standing object. The 3/4 contract does not apply to it. The column scan shows a repeating cycle of dark and mid tones with small light highlights and no top/front structure to judge. There is no standing body, no side face and no elevation to fail. The ground pattern reads as a plausible cobble or plate floor, so it passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and 26 per tile, so it is far richer. The paving reference has 7 colours and 7 per tile, so the candidate is close to it. The dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the tones lean neutral grey with no clear tint. The repeating bump pattern with highlights gives some texture and there are no flat fills. The pattern is very regular and tiled, so it looks mechanical beside the grass, which is varied and irregular. Compared with the grass reference it is much lower in colour and density. Against the paving reference it is slightly lower and the shading is shallower. The step count is 5, which is below Beodeul's usual 5-6 per material, and the neutral near-black tones read as a sticker look. When in doubt, fail.
